faq.a: Abdulbari represents Arabic عبد البارئ, meaning servant of al-Bāriʾ (“the Creator/Originator”).

faq.q: What is the origin of Abdulbari?
faq.a: The name is Arabic and is a compound of عبد and البارئ.
Yes. The underlying compound is عبد البارئ (ʿAbd al-Bāriʾ).

faq.q: What is the root of Abdulbari?
faq.a: عبد is related to ع ب د; البارئ is related to ب ر أ, associated with creating or bringing into being.
Abdulbari is a traditional Muslim personal name because it contains a compound invoking al-Bāriʾ, a divine epithet in Islamic tradition.
This record does not establish Abdulbari as an explicitly named Qur'anic person; the compound's religious meaning is distinct from personal-name attestation in the text.

faq.a: In Urdu, the name means servant of al-Bāriʾ, the Creator/Originator.
The supplied “ab-dul-ba-ri” is an approximate pronunciation; local pronunciations vary.

faq.a: The record classifies Abdulbari as masculine, consistent with traditional usage; regional frequency data is not supplied.
